description: Canonical machine-readable declaration of the operator.toml key set. Single source of truth for which keys exist, their type, their default-or-none, and whether the generator delivers them. docs/scripts/setup-workspace.sh derives write_operator_toml's emit and read_operator_toml's token map from this file; core/deploy/tools/check-operator-toml-schema.sh lints the template against it and reports an instance whose key set is behind. Adding a key is one object here and zero lines of code. See core/ADRs/ADR-140-operator-toml-declared-schema.md.

conventions.delivery: A section or key with delivery 'delivered' is emitted by the generator into every operator.toml and is inside the reconciler's coverage set. 'opt-in' means the template documents it, the generator never writes it, and the reconciler never touches it. A key may override its section's delivery.
conventions.default: KEY-ABSENCE means no default. Never write "default": "" to mean 'no default' — the empty string is a legitimate, load-bearing default meaning 'resolve via the canonical default' (core/standards/depersonalization-spec.md §4 Read-source contract). A delivered key with a default is backfilled silently; a delivered key with required:true and NO default is prompted for, and takes the exit-66 path when non-interactive.
conventions.source: token = resolved from the bracketed token map at install; operator-or-default = ovd(), keep the operator's non-empty value else the default; literal = emitted verbatim from 'default'; declaration-version = rendered from this file's declaration_version.
conventions.coverage: This declaration covers ADD only. A rename, removal or retype is a breaking change: it bumps declaration_version and routes to guided recovery rather than silently mutating an operator-owned file.

sections.name: meta
sections.description: Schema provenance for this generated file.

keys.description: Breaking-change marker, equal to this declaration's declaration_version. Compared on reconcile: equal proceeds, live > declared refuses (the config was written by a newer platform than this clone), live < declared routes to guided recovery. Additive key additions do NOT bump it — per-key 'since' carries the additive history.
Marks the file as platform-managed.

sections.name: platform
sections.description: Platform-surface selectors. work_board is a deprecated alias retained per ADR-022 §3.

keys.description: DEPRECATED ALIAS, superseded by [adapters].ticketing. Retained — NOT removed — per ADR-022 §3, so no future cleanup drops it by omission. New consumers read [adapters].ticketing; when both are set and differ, [adapters].ticketing is authoritative.
Team-comms surface comms-writer defaults to. Empty means no platform-specific formatting — a legitimate default, not an absent one.

sections.name: automation
sections.description: Ambient-intake automation ceiling — the C0 keystone every ambient-intake child clamps to.

keys.description: CEILING, not a switch: effective autonomy is min(automation_level, per-action max). Emitted through ovd() so a deliberate "off" is never reset by a re-bootstrap.

sections.name: adapters
sections.description: Host-adapter selectors — the four external surfaces the platform integrates with. ADR-022 §1/§4 names this the #703 onboarding seam and gives each selector a v1 default.

keys.description: Repository-host adapter — where the git surface and code review live. v1 ships GitHub via the gh CLI; additional hosts are gated on their adapter tickets.
Ticketing adapter — the work-tracking surface the pipeline reads and writes. SUPERSEDES the legacy [platform].work_board.
Knowledge-base adapter — where reference content lives.
AI-tool adapter — the agent runtime the platform targets.

sections.name: methodology
sections.description: Global delivery-approach default. ADR-022 §1 / ADR-017 §S2 name methodology an operator.toml concern.

keys.description: The methodology archetype an install starts from when a project does not set its own delivery_approach. ONLY the global default plus the resolver fallback — the enum and its validation stay canonical in core/schemas/project-schema.md.

sections.name: session_retro
sections.description: Per-session self-retrospective. SHIPPED INERT — enabled=false means the registered Stop hook does nothing until the operator deliberately turns it on.

keys.description: Master switch for the automatic trigger. Shipped false — activation is a deliberate operator edit, never something a platform update does. Asking for the retro by name always works and ignores every setting in this block.
Warn-then-enforce shakedown posture for the hook.
Sampling band. The event log is append-only and permanent, so a row emitted for a session that taught nothing permanently dilutes the cross-session signal.
Tool-call floor a session must clear before the hook fires.
Turn floor a session must clear before the hook fires.

sections.name: projects
sections.description: GitHub Projects (v2) board identifiers. Opaque operator-specific values with no meaningful default — emitting six empty strings would be noise, so they carry NO default and stay opt-in. If a consumer ever lands, they become the first required-undefaulted prompt case.
